question: Can a completed one-shot module-installer watchface safely request deletion of itself?
callsite_evidence: sub_CA7D2E0 logs watchface_manager_delete_watchface, rejects a null id, and delegates to sub_CA642B0(id,1)
sub_CA63E14 resolves the watchface record by id, rejects deletion of the last usable watchface, and chooses another eligible watchface before deleting the active record
sub_CA63E14 removes the selected watchface directory and logs delete watchface success; sub_CA642B0 then refreshes/persists manager state
control_flow_evidence: active-watchface deletion first marks an alternative record selected and updates the current watchface manager pointer
the path rejects missing IDs and the last-watchface case rather than deleting arbitrary unregistered directories
ownership_analysis: The firmware watchface manager owns registry records, active selection and directory removal. Callers pass a borrowed stable id string for the duration of the synchronous call.
unsafe_assumptions: self-deletion after a /dev/canopus install write is statically recovered but not yet device-probed with a Lua installer still executing
a failed deletion must not roll back an already committed module install; the installer remains visible for manual cleanup
recommended_probe: Install a disposable signed module installer while at least two watchfaces exist, verify module state becomes INSTALLED/DISABLED and notification insertion completes, then verify the manager switches away and removes only the installer id.
